draft.title: Evidence-based treatments for phobia
card: CBT
Cognitive behavioural therapy helps a person spot and challenge catastrophic thoughts about the feared thing. They also practise new, less fearful behaviours.
Systematic desensitisation
The person learns to relax, then faces the feared thing in small steps, from least to most frightening. Relaxation cannot easily happen alongside fear, so the fear response weakens.
Other supports
Breathing retraining slows breathing to calm the body when fear rises. Regular exercise can lower general anxiety.
Medication
Benzodiazepines can reduce anxiety for a short time. They are used briefly and carefully, as they do not remove the cause of the phobia.
draft.remember: Treatments help the person face the fear in manageable ways, and medication is only a brief support.

opts: Gradual exposure to the feared thing while relaxed
Challenging catastrophic thoughts about the feared thing
Slowing breathing to calm the body during fear
Taking a drug to reduce anxiety for a short time
a.why: Systematic desensitisation pairs relaxation with small, step-by-step exposure. Challenging catastrophic thoughts describes CBT, which is a different treatment.
a.clue: Think of steps from least to most frightening.

b.q: Tariq fears dogs. His psychologist teaches him to relax, then shows him a dog photo, then a dog behind glass, then a calm dog in the room. Which treatment is this, and why does it work?
opts: Systematic desensitisation, as relaxation replaces fear
Systematic desensitisation, as it removes all his thoughts
CBT, as it mainly changes his catastrophic thinking
Medication, as it lowers his anxiety for a short time
b.why: Tariq relaxes and meets the feared thing in graded steps, which is systematic desensitisation. Relaxation cannot easily happen alongside fear, so the fear response weakens. CBT is tempting, but the case describes gradual exposure rather than challenging thoughts.
b.clue: Look at the order of steps and what he does first.

a.best: Gradual exposure to the feared thing while relaxed

b.best: Systematic desensitisation, as relaxation replaces fear

problems.detail: The remember line says medication is "only a brief support". The card says benzodiazepines "can reduce anxiety for a short time" and are "used briefly and carefully". The absolute "only" is stronger than the card's hedged wording.
